Doc: A.1 item 113 need not be documented (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:34452). cite.py: 'OK §9.3.14.3 (Life cycle for instance objects) The timing and algorithm ... is implementor-defined.'; 'OK §9.1.4 (Open mode) — For file connectors in an object when the object is deleted.' The adjudicator's mechanism ('per-object instance files are closed by a re-armed finalizer') is DEAD CODE. ~CobolObject (src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/CobolObject.cs) calls CobolFile.EnqueueInstanceClose → `_reg => RunUnit.Current.Files` (CobolFile.cs:17), and RunUnit.Current is `_current.Value ??= new RunUnit()` over an AsyncLocal (RunUnit.cs). The GC finalizer thread does not carry the mutator's ExecutionContext, so it MINTS AN ORPHAN RunUnit and enqueues there; FileRegistry.DrainPendingObjectCloses on the real run unit never sees the key. Proof harness /tmp/adj/refute/h/P.cs (references the built Cobol.Net.Runtime.dll; subclass calls __TrackInstanceFile, GC.Collect+WaitForPendingFinalizers): output 'finalizer-thread ambient: a DIFFERENT (orphan) RunUnit; orphan pending=1' / 'main-run-unit pending closes after GC = 0'. COBOL-observable: /tmp/adj/refute/gc2.cob (--std 2002): loop {NEW WCLS; method W does OPEN OUTPUT of its instance file gc.dat + WRITE (no CLOSE); SET A TO NULL; 1,500,000 throwaway NEW JCLS} → 'K=00000002 OPEN-OUTPUT=61' — the second object's OPEN is refused as a sharing conflict by the first, unreachable object's connector, and stays refused forever. /tmp/adj/refute/gc1.cob: after dropping the writer and ~4M allocations, main OPEN INPUT of gc.dat → READ=10 (the record 'AAA' never flushed; the connector was never closed). So an object the runtime HAS determined cannot take part (its finalizer ran) is never destroyed as COBOL observes destruction (§9.1.4's implicit CLOSE 'when the object is deleted') until run-unit end, and FileRegistry keeps every minted per-object connector (and its OS handle) alive for the life of the run unit — unbounded growth for programs creating file-owning objects. §9.3.14.3 sentence 1 requires destruction 'when it is determined'; the §9.1.4 NOTE licenses GC delay, not a close that can never happen. Run-unit-end CloseAll still closes them (the 'whichever occurs first' backstop holds), and file-less objects are reclaimed correctly by the GC — hence PARTIAL, not DIVERGES.
